title: Design consistent progressive-disclosure patterns for toggles and dependent field validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Inputs that are revealed or required by toggle groups (e.g., ‘Enable advanced options’ or conditional billing address fields) currently use inconsistent validation timing, helper placement, and microcopy across the design system. Developers implement ad-hoc behaviors: some fields validate on blur, some only on submit, and helper text shifts cause layout jumpiness. This results in confusing UX (unexpected error banners when toggles are flipped), accessibility issues (focus loss and missing aria-live announcements), and inconsistent spacing/token use across components.

Goal: Define a single, accessible pattern for progressive-disclosure scenarios that covers: toggle-driven requiredness, on-toggle validation behavior, helper/validation stacking, focus and aria-live behavior, and token rules for vertical rhythm when fields are inserted/removed. Provide clear API/props guidance for the component library so engineers can implement predictable, composable behavior across forms (hosted API settings, billing flows, onboarding).
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc with behavioral matrix: for each toggle interaction (enable, disable, flip), describe expected validation timing (instant/blur/submit) and UI outcome
Figma component variants that show: empty collapsed toggle state, expanded fields with helper + success + error states, tokenized spacing for compact/regular density
Accessibility checklist mapping ARIA attributes (aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-required, aria-live) to scenarios and a short code snippet demonstrating usage
Developer guidance page (Confluence + storybook knobs) with examples: billing address reveal, advanced settings toggle, multi-select reveal patterns
Unit test/QA checklist for engineering: focus preservation when toggles expand/collapse, no unexpected validation pops on enable, proper announcement of new error messages by screen readers
decisions: Validation timing standard: newly exposed fields validate on blur and on submit; toggling 'enable' will not immediately surface errors unless the field was previously in error state
When a toggle disables a field, any existing validation errors are persisted in the form state but visually hidden; re-enabling restores visible errors if present

Helper text and error messages occupy a reserved assistive row to avoid layout shifts; tokens: spacing uses token vertical-space-2 between field and helper row, consistent across compact/regular densities

ARIA approach: set aria-expanded on toggle controls; aria-controls points to the container; newly revealed error messages must be placed in a container with aria-live="assertive" only when the error results from an action after expansion (not when simply revealing an already-existing error)
tasks: Audit current form components in storybook for toggle/conditional fields and document deviations (ENG-2025)
Create Figma variants for: collapsed toggle, reveal with neutral helper, reveal with inline error, reveal with multi-line helper stack (DES-77688-FIGMA)
Draft Confluence implementation guide with code examples for ToggleGroup and FieldRow APIs
Sync with engineering on required props: preserveErrorOnHide(boolean), validateOnToggle(boolean), liveRegionBehavior(enum)
Write accessibility test cases and attach to QA checklist
